newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON TO STAND DOWN IN THREE YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON TO STAND DOWN IN THREE YEARS.

text.p: Alex Ferguson, manager of Manchester United for the last 10 years, said on Thursday he intended to quit when his current contract expires in three years' time.

"I can see the finishing line," he said. "When this contract runs out I will be 58 and I can't see me continuing as manager beyond that. I have had it in my mind for some time that I would stand aside when I reached 58."

But Ferguson, who has guided United to two domestic doubles, an additional third league title and third F.A. Cup, the League Cup and the European Cup Winners' Cup, said he had no doubts he would see out his current contract.

"I committed myself to Manchester United for a further three years when I signed this contract and I will definitely see it through. I have completed 10 years at Old Trafford and I am as ambitious now as the day I arrived. You never become indifferent to success, or at least I don't.
"Every single day is important and that is how I will view this job until the time comes to step down."
Ferguson said he would like to take an advisory role at United when he stands down as manager.
